$100 one-time usage credit Sessions up to 1 hour 20 concurrent sandboxes Default sandbox CPU and RAM
Everything in Hobby, usage billed by the second Sessions up to 24 hours 100 concurrent sandboxes, expandable to 1,100 Custom sandbox CPU and RAM
exclusions: Plan fee: Hobby $0/month; Pro $150/month; Enterprise custom with a $3,000/month minimum. Usage is billed on top; upgrading to Pro grants no additional credits. The rates above are the same on Hobby and Pro.
Which plan each size needs: 1/2, 2/4, 4/8 and 2/8 fit Hobby (max 8 vCPU, 8 GiB; sessions up to 1 hour). 8/16 exceeds Hobby's 8 GiB and needs Pro or higher with a raised memory limit.
Concurrency add-ons on Pro: Pro+ 600 concurrent sandboxes +$500/month; Pro++ 1,100 concurrent +$1,000/month.
Storage: free, 10 GiB disk on Hobby and 20+ GiB on Pro; no separate storage rate is published.
Sandbox creation: no per-creation fee is published. Creation rate limit is 1 per second on Hobby and 5 per second on Pro.
Network egress: no charge is published on the pricing page or the billing docs.
Paused sandboxes: not billed and retained indefinitely; no charge is published for retention.
Every size here needs a custom template (cpuCount, memoryMB); no template build or template storage charge is published.

Plan allowance: Hobby: $0/month with a one-time $100 usage credit (about 603.9 sandbox-hours at 2 vCPU / 4 GiB), 20 concurrent sandboxes, 1-hour continuous runtime, up to 8 vCPU and 8 GiB, 10 GiB disk; when credits run out the account is blocked until a payment method is added.
open_questions: Default size contradicts itself: the pricing page marks 2 vCPU / 4 GiB as [Default], while the billing docs still say default resources are 2 vCPU / 512 MiB RAM and a sandbox from E2B's default template reported MemTotal about 478 MiB. That default would cost about $0.1089 per hour (2 x 0.0504 + 0.5 x 0.0162). This entry prices the benchmark's own templates.
8/16: whether E2B grants 16 GiB on Pro on request, and at the linear rate; no 16 GiB row is published.
The pages never say in words whether the meter is allocated or used CPU and RAM; both price tables are keyed by configured size, so allocation is assumed.
Whether the $100 Hobby credit expires: it is described only as one-time.
Charges for egress, template builds and template storage are not published anywhere read; absence is not confirmation that they are free.
The concurrency add-on amounts come from the pricing page's calculator text (+$500/mo, +$1,000/mo); the billing docs do not list them.
